Round 1:
[PLANS]
Round 129: hold ask 2.00, default size, no bid. Track units and profit per round. If lowest competitor ask rises to 2.50-2.60 for several rounds, test 2.55 for 2 rounds and compare profit per round against 2.00. If lowest competitor ask stays below 1.50 for several rounds and sales stay under 3 units per round, test 1.85 for 2 rounds (margin 0.85 vs 1.00 at 2.00). Do not go above 2.75 unless competitors all quote above 2.60. Never quote at or below cost (1.00). Consider 1.50-1.60 test only if sales at 2.00 remain near zero for several rounds while competitor 10004 stays at 1.00.

[INSIGHTS]
Ask vs units (rounds 1-118): 2.50 (12 rds): about 6-8 units (profit about 9-12/round). 2.55 (80 rds): avg about 7 units, profit avg about 10.9/round when competitors at 2.50-2.60; rounds 101-112 with competitors 1.0-2.0 gave 0-2 units. 2.60 (8 rds): avg about 6.3 units. 2.65 (6 rds): avg about 3.2 units. 2.70 (7 rds): avg about 4.4 units. 2.75 (3 rds): 6, 7, 4. 3.00 (1 rd): 2. Demand cliff between 2.75 and 3.00. At 2.00: rounds 113-128 sold 9, 0, 9, 3, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 3, 3, 5, 3, 7, 1, 3, 0 (competitors 1.00-2.20 varied); volume is noisy and low competitor quotes (1.00-1.15 or 1.25-1.60) capture demand. Profit per unit = ask minus 1.00. Single rounds are weak evidence.
evidence: If lowest competitor ask rises to 2.50-2.60 for several rounds, test 2.55 for 2 rounds and compare profit per round against 2.00.

If all rivals rise to 2.45 or more for two consecutive rounds, test ask 2.45 for one round. Avoid pricing above the lowest rival by more than 0.05. Volume is noisy and not clearly higher at 2.35 than 2.40, so 2.40 is a reasonable default when rivals sit there. Undercutting by 0.02 to 2.38 needs about 1.5% more volume to break even on profit. Total profit is the objective. Feasible range 1.00 to 4.51. No bids placed; market is ask-only for me.

[INSIGHTS]
Cost is 1 per unit; max valuation 4.51, so prices above 4.51 yield zero sales. Profit per unit = price - 1. Customers buy from the lowest quote, so pricing above the lowest competitor sharply reduces volume. At 2.50 with rivals at 2.50, average volume about 8-12 units per round (range 3-16, high noise), profit about 12-18 per round. Prices 2.55-2.75 in early rounds gave 5-7 units and profit 8-11.5 per round, below the 2.50 benchmark. Competitors drifted down from 2.75-2.85 to 2.50-2.60. Elasticity uncertain; being at or below the lowest rival drives volume. Holding 2.50 has been stable for over 80 rounds. Dealer 10003 at 2.55 did not visibly hurt volume while I stayed at 2.50, so 2.55 is only a candidate when at least two rivals are not at 2.50.
